scientific_question: Why do matched eco-genetic marginals with different cross-layer alignment produce different transitions and later functional-loss risks under the declared fragmentation dynamics?

mechanistic_hypothesis.analytic_identity: For S_j = alpha*q_j + beta*T_j + gamma*G_j, fixed layer-wise marginals fix mean(S) but not var(S); var(S) changes through covariance terms. In the locked aligned/anti construction T_j=G_j=B_j, so var(S)=alpha^2 var(q)+(beta+gamma)^2 var(B)+2 alpha (beta+gamma) cov(q,B).
mechanistic_hypothesis.directional_prediction: Positive alignment should increase spatial support variance and preserve a stronger upper-tail refuge under a rising barrier, whereas negative alignment should homogenize support and make all-patch realised high-trait loss more synchronous once the barrier approaches the common support range.
mechanistic_hypothesis.claim_boundary: The experiment tests this mechanism only for the declared finite closure and forcing path. It does not establish spatial heterogeneity as universally protective or cross-layer alignment as a universal risk score.

replication.paired_seed_mapping: same trajectory seed for all six conditions within each master-seed/replicate block

primary_mechanism_estimands: baseline support mean and population variance by condition
generation-specific maximum support and maximum interaction q
number of patches with realised high-trait occupancy
last-refuge loss time: first generation with zero realised high-trait occupied patches
paired functional-loss risk difference at generations 20 and 40
primary_comparisons: AA_full versus RR_full: total alignment mechanism
AA_full, AR_full, RA_full, RR_full: trait-alignment and allele-alignment factorial decomposition
AA_q_only versus RR_q_only: necessity of direct eco-genetic feedback into q for the alignment effect

decision_rules.support_variance_mechanism_supported: AA_full and RR_full have equal baseline support mean; AA_full has larger support variance exactly as predicted by the covariance identity; the difference persists in upper-tail refuge metrics before the later loss-risk separation.
decision_rules.refuge_path_supported: AA_full shows a larger or longer-lived upper-tail q/support refuge and later last-refuge loss than RR_full, in the same direction as the generation-20/40 loss-risk difference.
decision_rules.direct_q_feedback_necessary: AA_q_only versus RR_q_only removes or materially attenuates the AA-RR difference in q/refuge/loss metrics relative to the full-feedback comparison.
decision_rules.trait_vs_allele_decomposition: Use the four full-feedback factorial cells descriptively and with paired contrasts; do not relabel a post-result strongest cell as a new primary condition.

stop_rules: No new alignment permutations, barrier schedules, thresholds, endpoint definitions, weights, migration settings, or extra horizons may be added after outcomes are opened.
If q=0.625 is inconsistent with the declared z=1 viability equation in the pinned parent model, stop before simulation and report protocol invalid.
Do not infer universal ecological protection from support variance or refugia even if the declared model supports the mechanism.
